what_its_for: Dulaglutide is used to help control blood sugar levels in adults and children (10 years and older) with type 2 diabetes. It is also used to lower the risk of serious heart problems such as heart attack or stroke in adults with type 2 diabetes who already have heart disease or are at high risk for it. It is NOT used for type 1 diabetes or diabetic ketoacidosis.
how_to_take: Dulaglutide comes as a pre-filled injection pen that you inject under your skin (subcutaneously) once a week. You can inject it in your belly (stomach area), the front of your thigh, or the back of your upper arm. Change (rotate) your injection spot each week to avoid skin irritation. You do NOT need to mix or prepare the medication — the single-dose pen is ready to use. You can take it with or without food, and at any time of day. Try to take it on the same day each week.
dosing: The usual starting dose is 0.75 mg injected once a week. Your doctor may increase your dose to 1.5 mg once a week after 4 weeks if your blood sugar is not well controlled. The dose can be further increased to 3 mg and then up to 4.5 mg once a week if needed. Always follow your doctor's instructions and never change your dose without talking to them first.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember — but only if your next scheduled dose is at least 3 days (72 hours) away. If your next dose is less than 3 days away, skip the missed dose and take your next dose on your regularly scheduled day. Do not take two doses on the same day or within 3 days of each other. You can also change your weekly dosing day if needed, as long as it has been at least 3 days since your last dose.
storage: Store unused dulaglutide pens in the refrigerator between 36°F and 46°F (2°C to 8°C). Keep them in the original carton to protect from light. Do NOT freeze dulaglutide — throw it away if it has been frozen. Once removed from the refrigerator, the pen can be kept at room temperature (up to 77°F or 25°C) for up to 14 days. Throw away a pen after 14 days at room temperature even if it still has medication in it. Always check the liquid — it should be clear and colorless to slightly yellow with no particles floating in it. Do not use it if it looks cloudy, discolored, or has particles.
what_to_avoid: Avoid drinking too much alcohol, as it can affect your blood sugar levels. If you are also taking insulin or certain diabetes pills (like sulfonylureas such as glipizide or glimepiride), be extra careful about low blood sugar (hypoglycemia) — talk to your doctor about dose adjustments. Avoid driving or operating machinery if you feel dizzy or if your blood sugar is low. Do not share your pen with anyone else, even if the needle has been changed — this can spread infection.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor or get emergency help right away if you experience: severe stomach pain that does not go away (possibly spreading to your back), which could be a sign of pancreatitis; signs of low blood sugar such as dizziness, shakiness, sweating, confusion, or fast heartbeat; signs of a serious allergic reaction such as rash, itching, swelling of your face or throat, or difficulty breathing; a lump or swelling in your neck, hoarseness, or trouble swallowing (possible signs of thyroid problems); changes in vision or signs of diabetic eye problems (blurred vision); signs of kidney problems such as little or no urination or swelling in your legs; or if you feel your heart racing or pounding. Also tell your doctor if you experience ongoing nausea, vomiting, or diarrhea that is severe or does not go away.
when_it_works: Dulaglutide starts working right after your first injection, but it may take several weeks to see the full effect on your blood sugar levels. Most people notice meaningful improvements in blood sugar within 4 to 8 weeks. Weight loss, if it occurs, may be gradual over several months. Keep taking your medication as prescribed even if you feel well, because type 2 diabetes usually has no symptoms.
special_populations: Pregnancy: Dulaglutide is not recommended during pregnancy. Tell your doctor right away if you become pregnant or plan to become pregnant. Breastfeeding: It is not known if dulaglutide passes into breast milk. Talk to your doctor before breastfeeding. Children: Dulaglutide is approved for children age 10 and older with type 2 diabetes. Kidney or Liver Problems: Dulaglutide can generally be used in people with mild to moderate kidney or liver problems, but your doctor will monitor you closely. People with a personal or family history of a certain type of thyroid cancer (medullary thyroid carcinoma) or a rare condition called Multiple Endocrine Neoplasia syndrome type 2 (MEN 2) should NOT use dulaglutide. Always share your full medical history with your doctor.
